label: sound
instruction_covers: four handlers on_gain_focus, on_lose_focus, on_show, on_hide, each a constructor keyword and a read/write property mirroring the existing on_close handler
an unset handler still reads back as a callable no-op, matching the unset on_close convention including its wrapped handler
a firing handler is invoked with the window instance it belongs to
on_show fires on a not-visible to visible transition and on_hide on the reverse, whether changed through show()/hide() or the visible property, and a no-op request fires neither
minimizing a visible window fires on_hide and restoring it to a visible state fires on_show; other state changes and a state set that changes nothing fire nothing
a change of the application's current window fires on_lose_focus on the old window and on_gain_focus on the new one; setting the window that is already current fires neither
existing on_close behavior is left unchanged
notes: The test reads the wrapped handler's _raw attribute and drives focus through app.current_window and app.main_window and state through the WindowState enum. Both are the existing on_close mechanism and the public App/Window API that the instruction says to mirror, so they are visible in the repo rather than new contracts. The runner also executes the pre-existing tests/window and tests/app/test_app.py suites as a regression guard.
